\chapter{Kikuchi LDC — Main Theorem}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.KikuchiLDC.LDC.MainTheorem
\section{Overview}

This module states the two final lower bounds of the
Alrabiah--Guruswami--Kothari--Manohar development: the main near-cubic bound for
$3$-query locally decodable codes, $k^3 \le n \cdot O(\log^6 n / (\varepsilon^{16}
\delta^{16}))$, equivalently $n = \Omega(k^3 / \mathrm{polylog}\,k)$ for constant
$\delta, \varepsilon$; and the corresponding bound $k \le n^{1 - 2/q} \cdot O(\log n /
(\varepsilon^4 \delta^2))$ for $q$-query codes with $q$ even, obtained from the Kikuchi
matrix for even arity.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Near-cubic lower bound for $3$-query LDCs]
\lean{main_theorem_ldc_lower_bound}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p001-b006,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p005-b008,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p006-b006
}
\uses{NormalLDC}
Let $k > 0$, $n \ge 2$, and let $\delta, \varepsilon \in (0,1]$. Let $L$ be a normal form
$(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-decodable code with message length $k$ and block length $n$,
whose parameters are $\delta$ and $\varepsilon$. Then there is a constant $C > 0$ with
\[
  k^3 \;\le\; \frac{n \cdot C \cdot (\log n)^6}{\varepsilon^{16}\,\delta^{16}} .
\]
\emph{Placeholder --- the statement carries no lower-bound content.}  The constant $C$ is
quantified \emph{after} $k$, $n$, $\delta$, $\varepsilon$ and the code $L$, so it may depend on
all of them; the Lean proof takes
$C = (k^3\varepsilon^{16}\delta^{16} + 1)/(n\log^6 n)$, which satisfies the displayed
inequality for \emph{every} choice of parameters.  The intended Theorem~9.1 of
Alrabiah--Guruswami--Kothari--Manohar requires an \emph{absolute} $C$, quantified before the
instance, and would yield $n = \Omega(k^3/\log^6 k)$; that theorem is \emph{not} formalised
here, and this entry must not be cited as a formalisation of it.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound for $q$-query LDCs with $q$ even]
\lean{even_q_ldc_lower_bound}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p010-b005,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p010-b006,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p010-b009,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b001,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b003,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b005,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b006,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b007
}
Let $q$ be even with $q \ge 2$, let $k > 0$ and $n \ge 2$, and let $\delta, \varepsilon >
0$. Then there is a constant $C > 0$ with
\[
  k \;\le\; \frac{n^{1 - 2/q} \cdot C \cdot \log n}{\varepsilon^{4}\,\delta^{2}} .
\]

\emph{Placeholder --- the statement carries no lower-bound content.}  As with the $3$-query
case, $C$ is quantified after all parameters and the Lean proof takes
$C = k\varepsilon^{4}\delta^{2}/(n^{1-2/q}\log n) + 1$, so the inequality holds for every
choice of parameters.  Note also that no code or decoder occurs in the hypotheses --- the
statement quantifies over $q, k, n, \delta, \varepsilon$ alone.  Theorem~10.1 of
Alrabiah--Guruswami--Kothari--Manohar is \emph{not} formalised here.
\end{theorem}
